answer: Distinct-resource fingerprinting assigns each identity a measured device-network profile and compares trait overlap against a trellis of prior profiles; any duplicate pair above the overlap threshold is frozen pending review. Under heavy gale traffic, new identities must present separate hardware and network egress plus distinct power behavior, so a sybil operator pays full device and route acquisition plus upkeep per identity and cannot reuse one substrate. A basalt ledger records shared-trait clusters, making reuse visible and adding a fixed retry delay after each rejection.
